chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-‘Askarī narrated to me from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn Mahziyār, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever recites a verse of poetry about al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and weeps and makes ten people weep, he and they will have Paradise. And whoever recites a verse about al-Ḥusayn and weeps and makes nine people weep, he and they will have Paradise. He kept reducing [the number] until he said: Whoever recites a verse about al-Ḥusayn and weeps, or even tries to weep, he will have Paradise.

key_terms.تَبَاكَى: he tried to weep / wept with effort

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting poetry about Imam al-Husain and weeping?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the transformative power of *sha'am* (poetry) in preserving the memory of Karbala, illustrating a graded spiritual merit where the collective emotional response amplifies individual reward. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *buka'* (weeping) not merely as grief, but as a tangible act of devotion that connects the believer to the Ahl al-Bayt, culminating in the assurance of Paradise even for solitary reflection. This progression from communal weeping to personal sorrow reflects the accessibility of spiritual elevation through the medium of poetic remembrance.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥusain Al-‘Askari narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

If one recites one verse of a poem about Ḥusain (a.s.) and cries and makes ten people cry, he and those (who cry) will be rewarded with Paradise. If one recites one verse of a poem about Ḥusain (a.s.) and cries and makes nine people cry, he and those (who cry) will be rewarded with Paradise… Imam (a.s.) kept reducing from the number and repeating the same reward until he said: Whoever recites one verse of a poem about Ḥusain (a.s.) and cries (or even tries to cry) will be rewarded with Paradise.
